name: default
label: Default models (world: R1 10, run 2)
note: The default since section 6.13: the second R1 = 10 world run above the standard refiners. Look for island arcs, trenches, rifts and coastal ranges at level 0. Long rivers and continuous ridges are still missing when you zoom in.

name: old_default
label: Previous default world (R1 10, run 1)
note: The world model behind figures 2 to 14. Its level 0 is too rough (slope ratio 1.20): bumpy highlands, some round, domed continents and few trenches. With the standard refiners below, two errors cancel and the finest level gets about the right slopes.

name: world_slow
label: Slow latent field world
note: Level 0 with an extra latent field that changes over about 7,600 km. Worlds now differ in overall character, from almost pure ocean to land-rich (try other seeds), but with speckled shallow flats and sharp-edged plateaus.

name: single
label: Single scale, 20k steps
note: One generator trained directly at 0.93 km per pixel: the same look everywhere, with land and sea alternating every 100 km or so. Local runs only.

name: local_blur
label: Previous default world, blurred-input local refiner
note: The level-2 refiner trained on blurred coarse input. Zoom in fully and compare with the previous default: ridges are sharper, but on this rough level 0 the finest level is too rough (1.27) and has more closed depressions.

name: r1_40
label: R1 40 world
note: Gradient penalty 40 instead of 10: broad lowland plains, wide shallow shelves and fewer domed continents, but speckled flats along some coasts.

name: r1_80
label: R1 80 world
note: The strongest gradient penalty: level 0 slopes come closest to real, but mountains and mid-ocean ridges fade. Below it the cascade is too smooth (0.68), showing the refiners' own detail deficit.

name: r1_80_blur
label: R1 80 world, both blurred-input refiners
note: A smooth level 0 with both refiners trained on blurred input: the level-2 statistics closest to real in section 6.12 (slope ratio 1.03, height distance 104 m). Sharp ranges, plains and archipelagos, but a blurry, ridge-poor sea floor and more closed depressions.

name: r1_80b_blur
label: R1 80 world, run 2, both blurred-input refiners
note: A second R1 80 run under the same refiners: level 0 differs only slightly from run 1, but level 2 comes out too smooth (0.84). The refiners amplify small differences in level 0.

name: r1_60_blur
label: R1 60 world, both blurred-input refiners
note: R1 60 is no smoother than R1 40: large bumpy plateaus at level 0, and a level-2 slope ratio of 1.12.

name: r1_40_blur
label: R1 40 world, both blurred-input refiners
note: Too rough at the finest level (1.15): the blurred-input refiners add more detail to every input, so they only suit a smooth level 0.

name: r1_40b
label: R1 40 world, run 2
note: Same settings as the R1 40 run of section 6.11, another random start, and much rougher (level-0 slope ratio 1.42 against 1.13). Training runs differ about as much as the settings do.

name: r1_10c
label: R1 10 world, run 3
note: Same settings as the default, another random start. Best level 0 by SWD (60 against 110), with broad plains and continental shelves. Zoom in: the finest level is too flat, with few mountains (slope ratio 0.78).

name: r1_10c_regblur
label: R1 10 world, run 3, blurred-input regional refiner
note: Run 3 with the regional refiner trained on blurred input. It restores the slopes at the finest level (0.90) and lowers its SWD to 83, but adds closed depressions (10.4% of land).

name: r1_10d
label: R1 10 world, run 4
note: The fourth run with the default settings. Best level-2 SWD so far (76), but too smooth at level 2 (0.82), with 10% of land in closed depressions. No run won on every measure.

name: regional_pixelnorm
label: Regional refiner with pixel norm
note: The first regional refiner, with worm-like artefacts everywhere, including the sea floor, while its roughness score looked healthy. Local runs only.
